topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: I scarce can breathe when I see the thin, bent band, worn smooth as the stones in the river, in the pawnbroker's display. It's my grandmother's ring, the one she never took off till the day she was laid to rest. How did it come to be here? It's not a thing for the market, nor the miller's debt. I must have it back, for the sake of her memory, and the stories she told by the hearth. I will ask the lord for the coin to ransom it, though I know not how I'll repay, save by the sweat of my brow and the will of the saints. The soil may be stingy, but a man's honor is his richest crop.
